newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission aims for Balkans energy link-up.
newsitem.headline: Commission aims for Balkans energy link-up.

text.p: The European Commission announced on Thursday the creation of a task force which will seek to help boost energy cooperation in the politically sensitive Balkan region.
"Because of the crucial location of the Balkans in terms of international energy links, they are of special importance to the European Union," the EU executive said in a statement.
"They could form a focus of development in the context of political and economic cooperation," it said.
The task force will be responsible for coordinating investment projects to link together gas, electricity and oil networks in the Balkans. Within a year, it is to set up a list of priority projects.
"The task force will endeavour to facilitate the financing and implementation of energy networks in the Balkans and their interconnection with trans-European energy networks," it said.

EU Energy Commissioner Christos Papoutsis underlined the economic importance of the programme for the Balkans as well as for the 15-nation EU, saying it could help promote peace and stability and economic and social development.
Five nations -- Greece, Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania and Albania -- will participate in the task force together with the Commission.
Paputsis said the countries of the former Yugoslavia would also be welcome. However, so far only Bosnia and Macedonia had shown an interest.
"All countries in the area would be most welcome," he told a press conference, declining to give any figures of the investments that may be needed.
The Commission underlined the importance of energy cooperation between East and West.
